extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media relations professionals, donors, partners and the general public seeking WFP news
extracted.subtask_description: Formatting and content conventions used in World Food Programme (WFP) news releases — the elements, tags and phrasing WFP consistently uses when publishing announcements, funding notices, situation updates, and appointment/partnership news. Useful for writing or evaluating WFP-style humanitarian press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item label: 'News release'
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry is explicitly labelled as a 'News release' at the top of the item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page consistently shows the classification 'News release' for items; use this label to identify official WFP announcements distinct from blog posts, statements, or backgrounders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date
rubrics_metrics.description: Every release shows a clear publication date (e.g., '| 16 April 2026', '8 May 2026').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a visible publication date near the headline or label for chronological context and media citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline / title
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise descriptive headline summarises the main news (examples: 'WFP Releases HungerMap Live; a Modernized Intelligence Platform that Turns Data on Global Hunger into Early Action', 'Three years of war: Sudan's people abandoned and hungry').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines should be specific, news-focused and capture the core subject (product launch, funding, crisis update, appointment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and location formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases begin with a dateline indicating city and country in uppercase or headline case followed by a dash (examples: 'NEW YORK –', 'ROME, Italy –', 'DHAKA, Bangladesh -', 'MOGADISHU, Somalia -').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear dateline (city, country) followed by an em/en dash to set off the lede; maintain consistent punctuation/spacing for readability and newsroom conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede paragraph summarising key facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The opening paragraph immediately summarises the essential news: who (WFP/partners), what (contribution, activation, launch), where, why and often numbers or immediate impacts (e.g., 'The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) welcomes a contribution of EUR 10 million...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a strong lede that states the core news and provides the most newsworthy facts so journalists can quickly understand and report the item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical tags / themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each release displays topical tags or themes beneath the summary (examples: 'Hunger', 'Funding', 'Disaster risk reduction & anticipatory actions', 'School meals', 'Nutrition').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply clear subject tags to facilitate filtering and help readers/searchers find relevant releases by theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic tags / country list
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases list the countries or regions they concern (examples shown near items: 'Somalia', 'Bangladesh', 'Ethiopia', 'Cameroon').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include one or more geographic tags to identify affected countries/locations; useful for country desks, donors and local media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantified figures and beneficiary counts
rubrics_metrics.description: News items regularly include precise figures (currency amounts, metric tonnes, beneficiary counts) such as 'EUR 10 million', 'US$1.1 million', '22,600 vulnerable people', '390,000 people over the next 18 months'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific, verifiable numbers (funding amounts, beneficiary numbers, tonnages, dates) to communicate scale and impact; where possible give timeframes and geographic scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor and partner acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases explicitly name and thank donors, governments and partners (examples: 'welcomes a contribution of EUR 10 million from the Government of Spain', 'thanks the Governments of Belgium, Canada, France...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge funding sources and implementing partners by name and, when relevant, note what the funds will enable; this is important for transparency and donor relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes, attribution and transcript notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases include quoted material and explicit attribution conventions (e.g., 'This is a summary of what was said by the World Food Programme’s (WFP) Assistant Executive Director, Matthew Hollingworth, to whom quoted text may be attributed – at a press briefing in Geneva today.'; 'WFP Note to Correspondents' and transcripts are used to show what was said).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly whether quoted text is a verbatim transcript or a summary, provide the speaker's name and title, and include a 'Note to Correspondents' when publishing speeches or briefing summaries to indicate attribution rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulleted key-fact summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Some releases include bulleted lists highlighting program components, key outputs or emergency preparedness measures (example bullet list under 'New contribution from the United States strengthens WFP's emergency response in Haiti').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short bullets to present essential facts or program highlights for quick scanning by journalists and partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement-type clarity (action/status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases clearly state the nature of the action or status: activations ('WFP has activated its anticipatory action (AA) response'), launches ('released its next-generation platform, HungerMap Live'), appointments ('WFP appoints... as its newest global Goodwill Ambassador'), or warnings/alerts ('WFP projects food insecurity could reach record levels').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly frame the release as an activation, launch, appointment, warning or funding announcement so the reader immediately understands the type of news and potential follow-up actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of executive/official voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Many items highlight statements or summaries from senior officials (e.g., Executive Director, Director of Emergency Preparedness and Response) and designate whose words may be attributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify senior spokespeople and attribute statements to them to lend authority; include guidance on whom media may quote (attributable summaries vs full transcripts).
